sentences.text:
This writ petition is filed seeking for following reliefs:
(i) Issue an order, direction or writ in nature of writ of mandamus, directing respondents no.3 to 5 to re- determine and pay compensation with all benefits including interest from date of taking possession till payment in respect of land in Sy.no.204 measuring 3 acres 19 guntas of Kyalanur Village, Kolar Taluk under Section 24 of the Right to Fair Compensation Act, 2013 by considering representation as per Annexure-A dated 14.03.2022 etc.
2.
sentences._hearing_file: Smt Munirathnamma vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2023.json

sentences.text:
Sri Amar Gowda K.S., learned counsel for petitioners submitted that petitioners'
father-Narayanappa was tenant of land bearing Sy.no.204 measuring 3 Acres 19 guntas of Kyalanur Village, Kolar Taluk.
sentences._hearing_file: Smt Munirathnamma vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: Said land was subject matter of acquisition by respondents under Preliminary Notification dated 14.06.1978 for purposes of construction of school by respondent no.5.
sentences._hearing_file: Smt Munirathnamma vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: It was submitted that Final Notification was issued on 31.05.1979 and award was passed on 14.03.1980 determining total compensation of Rs.19,262.50/- as per Annexure-D.
sentences._hearing_file: Smt Munirathnamma vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2023.json

sentences.text:
But Village Panchayath,
Kyalanur had deposited NC: 2023:KHC:45187 only Rs.7,992.25/- out of total amount of Rs.21,188.75/- and therefore petitioners' father was not paid compensation.
sentences._hearing_file: Smt Munirathnamma vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: 3. It was submitted that petitioners' father was granted occupancy rights by Land Tribunal on 03.02.1982.
sentences._hearing_file: Smt Munirathnamma vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: In view of same, petitioners' father was entitled for compensation.
sentences._hearing_file: Smt Munirathnamma vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2023.json

sentences.text:
However,
respondents did not either deposit compensation nor pay it to petitioners' father.
sentences._hearing_file: Smt Munirathnamma vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: Therefore petitioners had submitted a representation on 14.03.2022 at Annexure-A before respondent no.3.
sentences._hearing_file: Smt Munirathnamma vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2023.json

sentences.text:
Despite lapse of time, same was not considered and therefore sought for allowing writ petition by issuing necessary direction for its consideration.
4.
sentences._hearing_file: Smt Munirathnamma vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: On other hand, learned AGA appearing for respondents no.4 and 5 submitted that even as per petitioners, cause of action for seeking compensation arose way back in year 1980 after passing of award and upon grant of occupancy rights in favour of their father.
sentences._hearing_file: Smt Munirathnamma vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: It was submitted that petitioners had earlier filed W.P.no.13567-13570/2012 seeking for restoration of their lands.
sentences._hearing_file: Smt Munirathnamma vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: Said writ petition was dismissed by order dated 16.03.2017.
sentences._hearing_file: Smt Munirathnamma vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2023.json

sentences.text:
Thus, petitioners having failed to seek for payment NC:
2023:KHC:45187 of compensation in earlier writ petition, were estopped from approaching this Court once again by filing fresh writ petition.
sentences._hearing_file: Smt Munirathnamma vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: 5. It was also submitted that in case petitioners wanted re-determination of compensation, they had remedy under Land Acquisition Act, but which had since been time barred.
sentences._hearing_file: Smt Munirathnamma vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2023.json

sentences.text:
6. Heard learned counsel and perused writ petition records.
7.
sentences._hearing_file: Smt Munirathnamma vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2023.json

sentences.text:
From above submission, it is seen that main grievance of petitioners is that though land in respect of which petitioners' father had filed application for grant of occupancy rights was acquired by respondents for construction of Government School, and award was passed in year 1980,
compensation was neither deposited nor paid and though petitioners submitted representation at Annexure-A, same was not considered.
sentences._hearing_file: Smt Munirathnamma vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: 8. Contention of learned AGA that there was delay and latches on part of petitioners in approaching Court and dismissal of their earlier writ petitions do appear substantial.
sentences._hearing_file: Smt Munirathnamma vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2023.json

sentences.text:
But when specific assertion of petitioners is that despite their claim for compensation on account of grant of occupancy rights by Land Tribunal, was not considered by respondents and NC: 2023:KHC:45187 compensation paid,
which would be violative of right to property, this Court finds it appropriate to direct respondent no.3-SLAO to consider petitioners' representation at Annexure- A, in accordance with law in a time bound manner in case petitioners substantiate their claim with appropriate records.
sentences._hearing_file: Smt Munirathnamma vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: 9. Hence, writ petition stands disposed of.
sentences._hearing_file: Smt Munirathnamma vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: Petitioners are permitted to supplement their representation at Annexure-A with appropriate records such as order of Land Tribunal granting occupancy rights etc., within one month from date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
sentences._hearing_file: Smt Munirathnamma vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2023.json

sentences.text:
Thereafter, respondents to consider same after verifying that 1) land in respect of which petitioners'
father had filed application claiming occupancy rights was acquired;
2) petitioners were entitled for compensation and 3) compensation was either not paid or deposited,
within three months thereafter, if necessary by seeking further information from petitioners.
sentences._hearing_file: Smt Munirathnamma vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: It is clarified that respondent no.3 would be obliged to inform result of consideration to petitioners.
sentences._hearing_file: Smt Munirathnamma vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2023.json

sentences.text: Needless to observe that direction issued to consider representation shall not be construed as a positive direction to grant relief sought in representation, but only as a direction to consider representation on its own merit in accordance with law within time limit set.

opennyai_summary.12_December_2023__facts:
This writ petition is filed seeking for following reliefs:
(i) Issue an order, direction or writ in nature of writ of mandamus, directing respondents no.3 to 5 to re- determine and pay compensation with all benefits including interest from date of taking possession till payment in respect of land in Sy.no.204 measuring 3 acres 19 guntas of Kyalanur Village, Kolar Taluk under Section 24 of the Right to Fair Compensation Act, 2013 by considering representation as per Annexure-A dated 14.03.2022 etc.
2.
Said land was subject matter of acquisition by respondents under Preliminary Notification dated 14.06.1978 for purposes of construction of school by respondent no.5.
3. It was submitted that petitioners' father was granted occupancy rights by Land Tribunal on 03.02.1982.
In view of same, petitioners' father was entitled for compensation.
However,
respondents did not either deposit compensation nor pay it to petitioners' father.
Therefore petitioners had submitted a representation on 14.03.2022 at Annexure-A before respondent no.3.
On other hand, learned AGA appearing for respondents no.4 and 5 submitted that even as per petitioners, cause of action for seeking compensation arose way back in year 1980 after passing of award and upon grant of occupancy rights in favour of their father.
opennyai_summary.12_December_2023__arguments: 8. Contention of learned AGA that there was delay and latches on part of petitioners in approaching Court and dismissal of their earlier writ petitions do appear substantial.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
But when specific assertion of petitioners is that despite their claim for compensation on account of grant of occupancy rights by Land Tribunal, was not considered by respondents and NC: 2023:KHC:45187 compensation paid,
which would be violative of right to property, this Court finds it appropriate to direct respondent no.3-SLAO to consider petitioners' representation at Annexure- A, in accordance with law in a time bound manner in case petitioners substantiate their claim with appropriate records.
opennyai_summary.12_December_2023__decision:
9. Hence, writ petition stands disposed of.
It is clarified that respondent no.3 would be obliged to inform result of consideration to petitioners.

opennyai_summary.final__facts:
5. The Coordinate Bench of this Court in W.P.No.36514/2024 (LA-KIADB), disposed on 05.02.2025, has held as follows:
NC: 2025:KHC:25147 HC-KAR "The petitioner claiming to be the absolute owner of land bearing Sy.No.60 (JMC Block No.22) measuring 1 acre situated at Bairadenahalli village, Kundanan Hobli, Devanahalli Taluka, Bengaluru District,
which has been acquired by the respondent-KIADB in terms of the provisions of Section 28 of KIADB act is before this Court seeking following relief:
"1) Issue writ of certiorari quashing the General Award bearing No.
KIADB/LAQ/626/2023-24 dated: 24.05.2023 passed by the Respondent No. 3 in respect of land in Sy.No. 60 (JMC Block No.22) measuring 1 Acre of land situated at Bairadenahalli Village, Kundana Hobli, Devanahalli Taluk, Bangalore Rural District,
in so far as the Petitioner is concerned, which is produced as ANNEXURE-E.
ii) Issue any suitable order, direction or writ in the nature of mandamus directing the respondent herein to consider the case of the petitioner for grant of developed land as per as per in the industrial layout formed by acquiring the land of the petitioner. on the lines of the G.O dated 13.05 2008 bearing No. CI 495 SPQ 2008 marked, as ANNEXURE-F, the G.O dated 13.08.2007 bearing No. CI 417 SPQ 2007 marked as ANNEXURE-G and the latest GO dated 23.02.2021 bearing No. 103 SPQ (E) 2019 marked as ANNEXURE-H.
iii) Pass such other order, writ or direction as the Hon'ble Court deems fit in the facts and circumstances of the case including costs."
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the general award has been passed.
However, in view of the government order dated 13.05.2008 produced at Annexures-F, G & H, the petitioner is also entitled for developed land in the industrial layout formed by the respondent-KIADB.
Hence,
seeks for quashing of the general award and for a direction to respondent-KIADB to consider his requisition/representation for allotment of developed land in lieu of the monetary compensation as per the government order dated 13.05.2008.
opennyai_summary.final__decision:
He submits if a representation in this regard is made by the petitioner, the same will be considered in accordance with law.
4. Submission is taken on record.
Accordingly, the following:
ORDER i) The writ petition is allowed.
 ii) The general award bearing  No.KIADB/LAQ/626/2023-24 dated  24.05.2023 passed respondent No.3 in respect of land bearing Sy.No.60 (JMC Block No.22) measuring 1 acre situated at Bairadenahalli village, Kundana Hobli, Devanahalli Taluka, Bengaluru District, is hereby quashed.
iii) The petition shall make a fresh representation within 30 days from the date of receipt of certified copy this order, thereupon the respondent-KIADB to consider the same in terms of the government order referred to in the writ petition at annexure-H.
iv) Such exercise shall be done with an outer limit of eight weeks from the date of submission of representation by the petitioner.
v) The respondent-KIADB is at liberty to withdraw the amount in deposit, if any."
In the light of the afore-quoted judgment and the identical facts, the petitioner is also entitled for the similar relief.
For the aforesaid reasons, the following:
ORDER i) The Writ Petition is allowed.
ii) Impugned General Award dated 11.07.2024, passed by the respondent No.3,
stands quashed qua the petitioner.
iii) The petitioner shall make a fresh representation within 30 days from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order, thereupon the respondent-KIADB to consider the same in terms of the Government Orders dated 13.08.2007, 13.05.2008 and Smt Munirathnamma vs The State Of Karnataka on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124596968/
4 23.02.2021 referred to in the writ petition respectively at Annexures-E, F and G.
iv)
Such exercise shall be done with an outer limit of eight weeks from the date of submission of representation by the petitioner.
v) The respondent-KIADB is at liberty to withdraw the amount in deposit, if any.
